mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to persistent discount rate expectations and reduced liquidity in the equity market.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day horizon, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying high-rate periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which tends to boost S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: During qualifying labor-market turning events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index) while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2.0 triggers a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals weak economic momentum and risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 AND CPIAUCSL < 200 for the same month
failure_condition: During qualifying supply shocks, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months and the Fed funds rate remains unchanged for three months, S&P 500 60-day forward returns tend to be positive due to reduced recession risk and accommodative market expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS unchanged for three consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market tightening coupled with policy restraint
failure_condition: During such regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (RSAFS) accompanied by a rise in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS) by more than 1% suggests labor market imbalances and tends to produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥10% in a month AND PAYEMS increases by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: During such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in consumer confidence (not available in the catalog) is proxy-ed by a downward trend in retail sales (HOUST) for four consecutive months, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to short-term risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for four consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon following the trigger, the forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% in a single month, without a corresponding increase in industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals supply-side disruption risk.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 300 AND INDPRO < 110 for the same month
failure_condition: During such inflation shocks, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).
